title: Game of Nim
summary: Alice and Bob play a game with n piles of stones.
statement: Alice and Bob play a game with n piles of stones. Alice starts. Each turn, a player picks a non-empty pile and removes any positive number of stones. The player who can't make a move loses. Given the number of stones in each pile, determine if Alice wins.
constraints: There are 1 through 7 nonempty piles, each containing 1 through 7 stones.
A move removes any positive number of stones from exactly one pile.
The player unable to move loses; both players play optimally.
hints: Each pile's Grundy value is its size because a move can reach every smaller size.
Combine independent piles with bitwise XOR.
A nonzero XOR lets the current player move to zero; every move from zero makes it nonzero.
Those paired invariants make zero-XOR states losing and every nonzero-XOR state winning under optimal play.
editorial: Those paired invariants make zero-XOR states losing and every nonzero-XOR state winning under optimal play.

tests.explanation: Alice removes the only stone and Bob has no move.
Whatever Alice removes, Bob mirrors by emptying the other pile, so Alice loses.
